## The specification menu {.smaller}

::: {.small .fs-75}
| Decision about the question | On the curve | Taught off the curve |
|:------|:--------------|:--------------------|
| **Frame set** | cosmopolitan, utilitarian, positive composite | the negative scales, on a curve of their own |
| **Scoring rule** | share of mentions | count, count per item |
| **Predictor, adjustment** | unemployment or growth, with or without the other | – |
| **Sample** | all 27 states, 2004–2013 | two periods, no bailout countries, no Greece and Spain |
| **Whose average** | each country-year once | by respondents, effective sample size, adult population |
| **Estimator** | two-way FE, country FE | random effects, pooled OLS, within–between |
:::

::: {.small .fs-75}
Seven more decisions, four of measurement and three about the model, make **fourteen**; their justifiable options cross into the **`r format(nrow(spec_curve), big.mark = ",")`** specifications of the curve. The [decision map]({{< var site-url >}}menu.html#map) gives the reason for every option.
:::

::: {.fragment .small .fs-75}
Two of these decisions already varied in the red-card study, where the 29 teams split across **four response distributions** (our outcome family) and **four ways of handling non-independence** (our estimator).
:::

::: notes
The menu lists every decision that anyone analysing this claim has to take, fourteen in all, and the slide shows the seven decisions about the question. They concern which framing scale is the outcome and whether it is scored as a share of the mentions of each respondent or as a count, unemployment or GDP growth, with or without the other measure beside it, which countries and years, whether each country-year counts once or in proportion to its people, and which comparison the estimator makes. Every option was reviewed with one question, whether it is a justifiable way to answer this claim. The middle column holds the options that passed, which, crossed with the options of measurement and of the model, give the eight hundred and sixty-four specifications of the curve, and the right-hand column the options that the workshop teaches beside it, with the reasons on the decision map. [advance] Two of these decisions varied in the red-card study already, where the twenty-nine teams split four ways on the distribution of the outcome, our outcome family, and four ways on the handling of observations that are not independent, our estimator.
:::

## Ground rules for the menu {#one-deviation-and-a-reason-for-it .smaller}

::: {.small .fs-85}
In Hands-on 4 the rule is: **change one decision at a time, and hold the others at the reproduced specification.**

The reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR in Hands-on 3: `mcosmo`; share of mentions; World Bank unemployment, raw; no adjustment; two-way FE; all 270 country-years; every country-year once; no mention scored zero; all 13 items; cells as interviewed; linear; CR2 errors clustered by country.
:::

::: {.fragment .small .fs-85}
Changing one decision at a time keeps the class chart **readable**: when a dot moves, you can say what moved it. An option that is off the curve is refused by `try_spec()`, with the reason and the page that teaches it.
:::

::: {.fragment .small .fs-85}
And one convention binds everyone: **claim-alignment**. Every scale on the curve is a positive framing, so below zero is the direction of the claim for unemployment; for GDP growth the sign is reversed, because the claim expects framing to rise with growth. The helpers apply it for you.
:::

::: {.fragment .small .fs-85}
The menu is the freedom that Task 2 of the robustness study left open. Its instructions fixed the outcome dimension, the predictor and the contextual variables of Model 2 and nothing else, not even the **unit of analysis**: two of the five analysts worked on respondents and three on aggregates, and their answers ran from *r* = `r fmt_num(max(five_r), 2)` to *r* = `r fmt_num(min(five_r), 2)`.
:::

::: notes
Two ground rules before you touch the menu. First, change one decision at a time and hold the others at the reproduced specification, my own model, with the settings listed on the slide and the CR2 test as its inference. The rule sounds restrictive, but it keeps the class chart readable, since we can then say what put a dot where it sits. [advance] An option that the review moved off the curve is refused by `try_spec()`, which says why and where the option is taught, and trying one is part of the exercise. [advance] Second, claim alignment binds everyone: every scale on the curve is a positive framing, so a negative sign supports the claim for unemployment, and for growth the helpers reverse the sign, because the claim expects framing to rise with growth. [advance] The menu is the freedom that Task 2 of the robustness study left open. Its instructions fixed the outcome dimension, the predictor and the contextual variables of Model 2 and nothing else, not even the unit of analysis, so that two of the five of us fitted models on respondents and three on aggregates, and five answers that all obeyed the instructions still ran from minus point zero six to minus point four five.
:::
